metadata.Name: BoolQ
metadata.Description: A dataset of naturally occurring yes/no questions.
metadata.Paper Title: BoolQ: Exploring the Surprising Difficulty of Natural Yes/No Questions
metadata.Venue Name: 2019 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
Affiliations: Paul G. Allen School of CSE, University of Washington
metadata.Abstract: Understanding what facts can be inferred to be true or false from text is an essential part of natural language understanding. In this paper, we study yes/no questions that are naturally occurring, meaning they are generated in unprompted and unconstrained settings. We build a reading comprehension dataset, BoolQ, of such questions and show that they are unexpectedly challenging. They often query for complex, non-factoid information and require difficult entailment-like inference to solve.
